Regarding $NVDA

The departure of the founder and CEO is a massive test for any company. Here are the reasons we expect $NVDA to continue to dominate:

💪 huge technological lead in chip design and supply chain control plus CUDA, that all survive a leadership change

💪 Engineering talent is deep. If Jensen was the chief designer of the chips and architecture, the company’s risk would be much greater 

💪 an ownership culture at NVDA: 80% of employees are stock millionaires and 50% own stock worth more than $25 million
These employees are not “punching the clock” and highly motivated to maintain the company’s leadership position 

💪 The stock has an attractive PE multiple and the substantial free cash generation means the company can support the stock via buybacks 

There will be pain near term since many investors view this as an adverse development. It is. But at 10x forward PE, this is also the best risk/reward in AI at the moment

US small businesses are signaling more inflation ahead:

The proportion of US small firms planning to raise prices over the next 3 months rose +6 percentage points in October, to 37%, the most since July 2022.

Excluding the post-pandemic surge in 2021 and 2022, this marks the highest reading since 2008.

By comparison, this figure did not exceed 30% between 2009 and 2019.

Furthermore, 33% of small firms raised prices over the last 3 months, the 3rd-highest reading since March 2023.

Meanwhile, 17% of business owners pointed to inflation as their single most important problem, up from 12% a year ago.

Small businesses are preparing for further price hikes as inflationary pressures mount.

US inflationary pressures are broadening:

Core CPI inflation surged to a 3-month annualized rate of +3.75% in October, its highest reading since April 2024.

This marks its 3rd consecutive monthly increase, up from +1.64% in July.

At the same time, core services less shelter inflation, also known as Supercore CPI and closely monitored by the Fed, rose to a 3-month annualized rate of +5.45%, its highest since mid-2024.

The weighted proportion of CPI components rising at an annualized rate above 2% soared to 76% last month, the largest percentage since August 2022.

This figure has risen +17 percentage points since July, marking its sharpest 3-month increase since early 2021.

The Fed's fight against inflation is far from over.

The late 1990’s internet analog would suggest that the AI boom is ending, but as I always caveat, price analogs are for “entertainment purposes” only. Then why show them at all, you might ask? Because looking at historical periods of similar price action can be an important conversation starter for how things might be the same or different this time. I use them as loose roadmaps, knowing that at some point the market may travel in a different direction. 

I had failed to realize this before last week, but the inflection point in the 1998-2002 analog was always going to be the midterm election. That could have been a hint that a regime change was in store.

Our message to Nvidia's board:

Do not fire Jensen Huang.

There is no clear replacement for Jensen Huang. We are confident that his departure would ultimately be a net negative for Nvidia, its shareholders, and the AI Revolution.

First, take a look at the data. History also suggests that removing a successful CEO will come with a significant cost.

A study of 187 forced CEO departures from S&P 1500 companies found that removing outperforming CEOs resulted in negative long-term stock returns. This case would be no different, in our view.

Jensen Huang is the definition of an outperforming CEO. Nvidia's board must not make a decision in the heat of the moment.

The board should take the time to conduct a thorough investigation and consult with shareholders, with a strong emphasis on the latter.

Quite literally, Nvidia's board should convene a special shareholder meeting and hold an advisory vote on this decision. This is the most consequential CEO controversy in world history. Shareholders deserve a say.

In addition, Nvidia's stock, $NVDA, is now down -35% in 26 trading days, nearly half of which is a result of the recent scandal.

We believe Jensen Huang's potential removal as CEO is now ~80% priced in.

Why take an action with massive downside potential when the market has already priced in much of that risk?

The downside of retaining Huang may be limited, while the potential upside is tremendous.

Lastly, history shows that retaining Jensen Huang could still lead to a favorable outcome. In 2019, Amazon retained Jeff Bezos as CEO after his extramarital affair became public, and the company's stock subsequently surged +108% by 2021.

Personal misconduct should not be ignored, but it must also be distinguished from corporate wrongdoing and weighed against the consequences of removing an executive who is instrumental to the company's success.

We believe Jensen Huang is an irreplaceable part of Nvidia and the AI Revolution more broadly.

Once the dust settles, firing Jensen Huang would prove to be a costly mistake.

It is time to pause and consult your shareholders.
